title: Dynamic watermark safeguard and tenant burst-hedge orchestrator
author: Samir Patel
release_notes: Introduce watermark-driven soft-eviction & probabilistic burst-hedge borrowing for Dedicated fleets; adds telemetry for per-tenant headroom and p95/p99 throughput guarantees. Backwards-compatible config defaults.
description:
Context and motivation: Customers have increasingly requested predictable throughput guarantees during sustained load while still allowing short, controlled bursts. The existing dedicated autoscaler only supports static reservation watermarks and global backpressure; that model either over-provisions for tail spikes or throttles aggressively during short bursts. This PR implements a dynamic watermark safeguard with a probabilistic burst-hedge borrowing mechanism and tenant-level headroom telemetry so the autoscaler can maintain percentile-based throughput guarantees without blowing committed capacity.

What this change does (summary):
- Introduces a WatermarkController that maintains per-tenant dynamic low/high watermarks based on recent utilization windows (configurable windows: 1m, 5m, 1h) and target percentile (p50/p95/p99).
- Adds a lightweight probabilistic Borrower that allows tenants to borrow soft tokens from a cross-tenant burst pool with credit accounting and exponential backoff on repeated borrowing. Borrow decisions are probabilistic to avoid synchronized spikes.
- Integrates watermark signals with the existing DedicatedAutoscaler decision path (hooked prior to provisioning API calls) so scale-ups are triggered only when sustained utilization crosses the high-watermark, while short bursts are served from the soft pool.
- Emits new telemetry metrics: tenant_headroom_bytes, tenant_burst_tokens_allocated, tenant_borrow_attempts_total, tenant_borrow_success_total, tenant_utilization_p95, and watermark_adjustment_events. These are tagged by tenant_id, region, and priority_tier.
- Adds CLI and Console config flags for enabling the dynamic watermark behavior per-tenant and an emergency throttle toggle for account-level hard limits.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc created and linked (ENG-6742).
- [x] Unit tests for watermark adjustment logic and Borrower sampler.
- [x] Integration test that simulates sustained load + microbursts to validate p95 guarantee.
- [x] Telemetry dashboards added (console JSON) and included in packaging.
- [x] Backwards-compatible config and migration notes.

Commits (high level):
- 1f3b9a2 add WatermarkController skeleton and interfaces
- b42c1d0 implement sliding-window percentile estimator and adjustment policy
- 7d4f2b9 probabilistic Borrower + accounting + tests

Files changed (high level):
- pkg/autoscaler/watermark_controller.go (new) - core control loop and adjustment policy
- pkg/autoscaler/borrower.go (new) - probabilistic borrow sampling and accounting store
- pkg/autoscaler/decision.go - integrate watermark guard into scale decision path (small diff)
- internal/telemetry/metrics.yaml - new metric definitions and tags

- cmd/redwoodctl/config.go - CLI toggles and config validation
- test/integration/dedicated_watermark_test.go - scenario based test exercising p95 guarantee

Small illustrative snippet (borrower probabilistic sampler):
- sampler uses a Poisson-based acceptance where P(accept) = min(1, base_rate * exp(-recent_borrow_count / decay)) so frequent borrowers see reduced acceptance and headroom is preserved. (See borrower.go:AcceptBorrow)

Review conversation (highlights):
- Priya Nair: "Nice overall design; the probabilistic borrow model is clever and should prevent thundering herd. Please add a short paragraph in the design doc about worst-case fairness and how we treat tenants hitting repeated rejections."
- Samir (author): "Added a fairness section and a new histogram metric to track repeated rejections per tenant; update pushed in commit c113d0a."
- Jordan Lee: "Integration tests are thorough. One nit: can we prefer immediate scale-up when a tenant is on a paid enterprise tier even if borrow acceptance is low? Otherwise they might experience degraded p95 despite having committed capacity."
- Samir: "Good call. Added a priority_tier bypass flag (configurable) so enterprise commits always trigger provision when high-watermark exceeded; added tests to cover bypass behavior."
- Omar Haddad: "CI flaked on the telemetry packaging job on first run. Rerun fixed it. Verified dashboards render in staging with sample data."

CI and checks:
- unit-tests: pass
- integration-tests: pass
- lint: pass (go vet/ineffassign addressed)
- telemetry-packaging: initially failed due to asset path mismatch; fixed in a follow-up commit and rerun: pass
- e2e-staging: pass (run against a 3-node dedicated fleet simulation)

Performance notes:
- Local bench against the serving runtime shows the watermark decision path adds ~0.7ms median latency to scale decision but no measurable per-request latency impact since borrow is resolved before request routing completes.
- Borrow accounting uses a bounded in-memory LRU keyed by tenant+window; memory overhead < 2MB per 10k tenants (configurable TTL).

Migration and rollout plan:
- Feature is off by default. Console toggle exposes two modes: experimental (probabilistic borrow only, no priority bypass) and enterprise (enables priority_tier bypass).
- Gradual rollout using per-tenant opt-in and canary group (5% of tenants -> 25% -> 100%) with monitoring alerts for increased rejection rates and p95 regressions.
- Rollback: toggle off in Console will cause Borrower to return zero acceptance and WatermarkController to revert to static watermark derived from config.

Backward compatibility and config:
- Existing reserved capacity semantics unchanged. New config keys have sensible defaults to keep behavior stable. There are no DB migrations; accounting uses ephemeral KV with eventual persistence to the usage ledger for billing reconciliation.

Follow-ups (future work):
- Extend borrower sampling to be cluster-aware for multi-region fleets.
- Expose tenant-level credit history in Console; link to billing for soft-borrow adjustments.
